```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)     # For polr (ordinal logistic regression)
library(lme4)     # For mixed-effects model
library(broom)    # For tidying model output
library(pROC)     # For ROC and AUC
```

## 📁 Data Loading and Cleaning

```{r load-clean}
setwd("~/Thesis")

#-------------------------------
#reading and cleaning the dataset
header_line <- readLines("ESS6e02_6.csv", n = 1)
column_names <- unlist(strsplit(header_line, ","))  

ess6 <- read.csv("ESS6e02_6.csv", sep = ",", header = FALSE,skip = 1,
                 col.names = column_names, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

colnames(ess6) <- gsub("^X\\.", "", colnames(ess6))     
colnames(ess6) <- gsub("\\.$", "", colnames(ess6))      

#-------------------------------
```
## ✅ Data Preparation for Modeling

```{r preprocessing}
# Clean and prepare the data for modeling
ess6_model <- ess6 %>%
  filter(!is.na(physact), !is.na(cntry)) %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert physical activity to ordinal (assuming 0-7 days is ordered)
    physact_ordinal = factor(physact, ordered = TRUE),
    
    # Create binary physical activity variable (active vs inactive)
    physact_binary = ifelse(physact >= 3, "Active", "Inactive"),
    physact_binary = factor(physact_binary, levels = c("Inactive", "Active")),
    
    # Clean other variables
    happy = ifelse(happy %in% c(77, 88, 99), NA, happy),
    hinctnta = ifelse(hinctnta %in% c(77, 88, 99), NA, hinctnta),
    agea = ifelse(agea == 999, NA, agea),
    gender_label = factor(gndr, levels = c(1, 2, 9), 
                         labels = c("Male", "Female", "No Answer"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(happy), !is.na(hinctnta), !is.na(agea), gndr %in% c(1, 2))
```
## 🔼 Ordinal Logistic Regression

```{r ordinal-model}
library(MASS)

ordinal_model <- polr(physact_ordinal ~ agea + gender_label + happy + hinctnta + cntry,
                      data = ess6_model, Hess = TRUE)

# Summary and interpretation
summary(ordinal_model)

# Calculate p-values and odds ratios
ctable <- coef(summary(ordinal_model))
pvals <- pnorm(abs(ctable[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
ctable <- cbind(ctable, "p value" = pvals)
odds_ratios <- exp(coef(ordinal_model))

# View results
print(ctable)
print(odds_ratios)
```

```{r}
library(lme4)

# simpler binary version
mixed_binary <- glmer(physact_binary ~ agea + gender_label + happy + hinctnta + (1 | cntry),
                     data = ess6_model, family = binomial)

# Model summary and interpretation
summary(mixed_binary)

# Calculate odds ratios and confidence intervals
fixed_effects <- fixef(mixed_binary)
odds_ratios <- exp(fixed_effects)
conf_int <- exp(confint(mixed_binary, method = "Wald"))

# View results
print(odds_ratios)
print(conf_int)
```
```{r}
# Compare model fit
AIC(ordinal_model, mixed_binary)

# Check variance explained by country (ICC)
library(performance)
icc(mixed_binary)
```
```{r}
# Model with quadratic age term
mixed_binary_quad <- glmer(physact_binary ~ agea + I(agea^2) + gender_label + happy + hinctnta + (1 | cntry),
                          data = ess6_model, family = binomial)

# Compare with linear model
anova(mixed_binary, mixed_binary_quad)

# Visualize the age relationship
age_range <- seq(min(ess6_model$agea), max(ess6_model$agea), length.out = 100)
pred_data <- data.frame(agea = age_range,
                       gender_label = "Male",
                       happy = mean(ess6_model$happy, na.rm = TRUE),
                       hinctnta = median(ess6_model$hinctnta, na.rm = TRUE),
                       cntry = "IE") # Using Ireland as reference

preds <- predict(mixed_binary_quad, newdata = pred_data, type = "response", re.form = NA)

ggplot(data.frame(Age = age_range, Probability = preds),
       aes(x = Age, y = Probability)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Probability of Being Physically Active by Age",
       subtitle = "Controlling for Gender, Happiness and Income",
       y = "Probability of Being Active") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Gender-income interaction
mixed_interaction <- glmer(physact_binary ~ agea + I(agea^2) + gender_label*hinctnta + happy + (1 | cntry),
                         data = ess6_model, family = binomial)

# Compare models
anova(mixed_binary_quad, mixed_interaction)

# Visualize interaction
interaction_plot <- ggplot(ess6_model, aes(x = hinctnta, y = as.numeric(physact_binary)-1, 
                                          color = gender_label)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), 
              se = FALSE, size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Income-Physical Activity Relationship by Gender",
       x = "Income Decile",
       y = "Probability of Being Physically Active",
       color = "Gender") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  theme_minimal()

print(interaction_plot)
```


```{r}
library(merTools)

# Plot country random effects
plotREsim(REsim(mixed_binary, n.sims = 500))

# Get country-specific predictions
country_preds <- predictInterval(mixed_binary, newdata = data.frame(
  agea = median(ess6_model$agea),
  gender_label = "Male",
  happy = mean(ess6_model$happy),
  hinctnta = median(ess6_model$hinctnta),
  cntry = unique(ess6_model$cntry)),
  level = 0.95, n.sims = 500)

country_preds$cntry <- unique(ess6_model$cntry)

# Plot country predictions
ggplot(country_preds, aes(x = reorder(cntry, fit), y = fit)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Country-Specific Physical Activity Probabilities",
       subtitle = "For median age, income and mean happiness (male respondents)",
       x = "Country",
       y = "Probability of Being Active") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
library(ggeffects)

# Create prediction plots for main effects
age_effect <- ggpredict(mixed_binary_quad, terms = "agea [all]")
gender_effect <- ggpredict(mixed_binary_quad, terms = "gender_label")
happy_effect <- ggpredict(mixed_binary_quad, terms = "happy [all]")
income_effect <- ggpredict(mixed_binary_quad, terms = "hinctnta [all]")

# Plot all effects together
library(patchwork)

(plot(age_effect) + labs(title = "Age Effect")) + 
(plot(gender_effect) + labs(title = "Gender Effect")) +
(plot(happy_effect) + labs(title = "Happiness Effect")) + 
(plot(income_effect) + labs(title = "Income Effect")) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```

```{r}
# Check if results hold when excluding countries with small samples
country_counts <- ess6_model %>% count(cntry) %>% filter(n > 100)
ess6_model_large <- ess6_model %>% filter(cntry %in% country_counts$cntry)

sensitivity_model <- glmer(physact_binary ~ agea + I(agea^2) + gender_label + happy + hinctnta + (1 | cntry),
                          data = ess6_model_large, family = binomial)

# Compare coefficients
cbind(Original = fixef(mixed_binary_quad),
      Sensitivity = fixef(sensitivity_model))
```
